runs.summary: AMD’s latest reported growth is led by Data Center, with strong demand and profitability evidence alongside weaker Client and Gaming performance. Production execution, demand conversion, competition, cyclicality, and valuation remain central uncertainties. Recent price behavior and the mixed broad-market backdrop offer limited evidence for a short-horizon directional view.

keyFindings.text: For the nine months ended September 26, 2026, consolidated revenue grew +44.3% YoY (9-month period ending 2026-09-26) year over year and gross profit grew +62.7% YoY (9-month period ending 2026-09-26). Operating income grew +224.3% YoY (9-month period ending 2026-09-26), amplified by the prior-year comparison base.

Data Center was the main growth engine. For the nine months ended September 26, 2026, issuer-reported segment revenue was $21.0B (9-month period ending 2026-09-26) and segment operating income was $6.6B (9-month period ending 2026-09-26). Segment operating margin was 31.3% (9-month period ending 2026-09-26), compared with 16.4% (9-month period ending 2025-09-27) a year earlier. The filing attributes growth mainly to EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs.

In Q3 2026, issuer-reported Data Center segment revenue was $8.5B (3-month period ending 2026-09-26), up 97% year over year. The filing attributes the increase mainly to demand for EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs; the earnings release also reports the MI450 launch and plans to scale Helios and Venice production.

Performance outside Data Center was less uniform. For the nine months ended September 26, 2026, issuer-reported Client and Gaming segment revenue was $11.2B (9-month period ending 2026-09-26), while segment operating income was $1.7B (9-month period ending 2026-09-26) and operating margin was 15.5% (9-month period ending 2026-09-26), versus 20.1% (9-month period ending 2025-09-27) a year earlier. Q3 Client and Gaming revenue declined 8% year over year.

At September 26, 2026, AMD reported cash of $7.4B (as of 2026-09-26), debt of $7.1B (as of 2026-09-26), net debt of $-8.7B (as of 2026-09-26), and a current ratio of 2.72x (as of 2026-09-26). These balance-sheet measures describe reported liquidity and leverage, not returns from future investment.

risks.text: Observed fact: AMD identifies rapid competition, semiconductor downturns, customer-market conditions, product-launch execution, seasonality, and potential loss of a significant customer among its risks. The 2025 10-K reported no customer at or above 10% of consolidated revenue in 2024 or 2025, but the supplied 2026 10-Q excerpt does not establish whether that remained true.

Observed fact: Data Center growth is significant, while nine-month Client and Gaming operating income and margin declined year over year. A change in Data Center demand, product mix, or delivery scale would therefore interact with weakness elsewhere in the business.

Observed fact: The November 3 close was below the 50-day average and above the 200-day average. Prior short-horizon calls on AMD’s range and relative performance resolved as misses, which supports caution about inferring near-term price behavior from recent moves alone.
Observed fact: The peer comparison has four usable peers, only one core peer, and excludes NVIDIA under the screen’s market-cap rule. It is a narrow reference for interpreting AMD’s revenue multiple.

catalysts.text: Observed fact: The Q3 2026 release reports plans to scale Helios and Venice production and states that Q4 revenue and earnings growth are expected to accelerate. Subsequent disclosures on shipments, supply, and Data Center margins would provide evidence on execution.

Issuer claim: The supplied Reuters report describes AMD’s forecast for Q4 2026 revenue of about $17 billion, plus or minus 3%, and 2027 revenue growth above 80%. These are company forecasts as reported by Reuters, not realized results.

Observed fact: The next earnings date in the supplied calendar is February 1, 2027, labeled provider-estimated and not issuer-confirmed; provider consensus estimates are also supplied. The next report could update evidence on growth and production execution.

keyFindings.text: Observed fact: For the six months ended June 27, 2026, consolidated revenue grew +44.1% YoY (6-month period ending 2026-06-27) year over year; gross profit grew +71.0% YoY (6-month period ending 2026-06-27). Operating income grew +415.8% YoY (6-month period ending 2026-06-27), from a low prior-year base.

Issuer claim: Data Center revenue for the six months ended June 27, 2026 grew 81% year over year, driven mainly by EPYC processors and Instinct MI350 Series GPUs. Second-quarter segment operating margin was 31.3% (3-month period ending 2026-06-27); the comparison with the prior year partly reflects the absence of MI308 export-control inventory charges.

Observed fact: First-half Client and Gaming revenue grew 13%, while its six-month segment operating margin was 15.5% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27), compared with 19.2% a year earlier. Embedded segment operating margin was 39.1% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27).

Derived calculation: Six-month operating cash flow from continuing operations was $5.321 billion and capex was $1.197 billion; the continuing-operations cash-flow-less-capex proxy was $4.1B (6-month period ending 2026-06-27). Continuing-operations operating cash flow grew +121.6% YoY (6-month period ending 2026-06-27) year over year, while capex outflow grew +142.3% YoY (6-month period ending 2026-06-27).

Observed fact: At June 27, 2026, AMD reported cash and short-term investments of $13.111 billion against debt of $3.226 billion. The supplied net-debt measure was $-9.9B (as of 2026-06-27), and the current ratio was 2.61x (as of 2026-06-27).

risks.text: Stale evidence: The latest supplied issuer financial results end June 27, 2026. They do not establish subsequent-quarter revenue, margins, shipments, or cash generation.

Observed fact: The prior-year Data Center margin comparison includes a period affected by MI308 export-control inventory charges. That comparison does not isolate underlying margin trends from the change in charges.
Missing required source: Supplied evidence does not quantify accelerator shipment economics, customer utilization, or Helios deployment scale.

Observed fact: The World Labs agreement is an approximately $8.2 billion stock transaction. Closing status, final share issuance, integration costs, and operating contribution remain unresolved in supplied evidence.

catalysts.text: Issuer-confirmed: AMD’s fiscal Q3 2026 results are scheduled for November 3 after market close. The report can provide operating evidence beyond the June reporting period; supplied EPS and revenue figures are provider estimates.

Observed fact: AMD and Meta announced an expanded strategic partnership on October 27 covering AI systems, processors, GPUs, networking, and software. The supplied announcement does not quantify future revenue or earnings contribution.
Observed fact: Further World Labs transaction disclosures could clarify closing status, share issuance, integration costs, and operating contribution.

Second-quarter segment operating margin was 31.3%, compared with -4.8% a year earlier; the comparison partly reflects prior-year MI308 export-control charges.
First-half segment performance was uneven. Client and Gaming revenue grew 13%, while its operating margin was 15.5%; Embedded segment operating margin was 39.1%.

For the six months ended June 27, operating cash flow from continuing operations grew +121.6% YoY (6-month period ending 2026-06-27) year over year, while reported capex outflow grew +142.3% YoY (6-month period ending 2026-06-27). catalysts.text: AMD is scheduled to report fiscal Q3 2026 results on November 3 after market close, an issuer-confirmed date. The report can update operating evidence beyond June; supplied estimates are provider estimates, not company guidance.

keyFindings.text: For the six months ended June 27, 2026, revenue grew 44.1% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27) year over year, and gross profit grew 71.0% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27). Operating income grew 415.8% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27), amplified by a low prior-year base.

Second-quarter segment operating margin was 31.3% (3-month period ending 2026-06-27), compared with -4.8% in the year-earlier quarter; the comparison partly reflects the absence of prior-year MI308 export-control charges.

For the six months ended June 27, operating cash flow from continuing operations grew 121.6% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27) year over year; capital expenditure grew 142.3% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27).
